title: WARN() in registry PBKDF2 backstop can halt module load on hardened kernels
description: Trigger: PBKDF2 provider registers with min_iterations<1000 on a kernel built with CONFIG_BUG_ON_WARN=y (common on hardened/FIPS kernels). WARN() may halt execution at insmod time, causing the provider module to fail loading entirely — the opposite of what a backstop should do. The framework already enforces the limits in ioctl_do_kdf; the registration check is defense-in-depth only and should not block load. Fix: replace WARN() with pr_warn() and restructure as explicit if-statements. src/provider/crypto2dev_registry.c:73-80
